title: DFT geometry optimization
action: Perform DFT geometry optimization of the title compound at the B3LYP level with the CEP-121G basis set, using the crystal structure from CCDC 254302 as the initial geometry. Save the optimized Cartesian coordinates as an XYZ file.
description: The optimized geometry is checked against experimental X-ray bond lengths via structural audit (RMSD tolerance).
output_schema: Standard XYZ format: first line number of atoms, second line comment, then each line: element_symbol x y z (in Å).

title: Vibrational frequency and bond order analysis
action: Using the optimized geometry from Step 1, run a harmonic vibrational frequency calculation at B3LYP/CEP-121G. Scale the computed frequencies by 0.96. Also perform a bond order analysis (e.g., Wiberg bond indices or NBO) to obtain numerical bond orders for the Hg–C and Hg–S bonds.
description: This step produces the scaled frequencies required for thermodynamics (Step 04) and the bond order data for Step 03. The evidence log records successful execution.

title: Bond order trend verification
action: Extract the computed bond orders for Hg–C and Hg–S from the analysis performed in Step 2 and write them to a CSV file.
description: The checker validates the bond order CSV output format.
output_schema: CSV with header: bond,order. Two rows: 'Hg-C',<value> and 'Hg-S',<value>.

title: Thermodynamic functions from vibrational data
action: Using the scaled harmonic vibrational frequencies from Step 2 and standard statistical thermodynamics formulas, compute the standard molar heat capacity (Cp), entropy (S), and enthalpy (H) at the temperatures: 200.0 K, 298.1 K, 300.0 K, 400.0 K, 500.0 K, 600.0 K, 700.0 K, 800.0 K. Output a CSV table.
description: This step forces genuine execution of the frequency calculation in Step 02. The checker compares the obtained thermodynamic values to hidden reference values with tolerances.
output_schema: CSV with columns: T (K), Cp (J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), S (J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), H (kJ mol⁻¹). Eight rows, one per temperature.

title: First hyperpolarizability (β_μ) by PM3
action: Using the optimized geometry from Step 01, perform a semi-empirical PM3 calculation (MOPAC) to compute the first hyperpolarizability β_μ along the dipole moment direction. Output the value in esu.
description: The checker compares the computed β_μ to a hidden reference value within a tolerance.
output_schema: CSV with columns: property,value. One row: property='beta_mu', value=<numeric>.

title: TD‑DFT electronic absorption spectrum
action: Run a TD‑DFT calculation on the optimized geometry at B3LYP/CEP‑121G level to obtain the two strongest electronic transitions. Output their wavelengths in nm and oscillator strengths.
description: The checker compares the computed wavelengths and oscillator strengths to hidden reference values within tolerances.
output_schema: CSV with columns: wavelength_nm,oscillator_strength. Two rows, one per transition.
